note: Atlas-authored rules of thumb (research spec sources.md section 4, general bar and kitchen practice). taste_shift values are deltas on the 0..5 taste scale (sweet, sour, bitter, salty, umami, fat, alcohol, astringency); aroma_shift values are deltas on the 0..1 aroma-family weights. A prepared ingredient is base vector + shift, clamped. Directional estimates for ranking and explanation, not measurements. matches lists the ingredient technique words that make this preparation available for an ingredient.

preparations.name: Fresh juice
preparations.notes: Loses peel aromatics, keeps fruit; sour and sweet concentrated, no pith bitterness. Citrus is best within about 4-8 hours.

preparations.name: Zest / expressed peel
preparations.notes: Peel oils only: aroma without liquid volume; bitterness only if pith is included.

preparations.name: Muddled
preparations.notes: Releases herb oils and juice; over-muddled herbs or peel turn green and bitter.

preparations.name: Grilled / charred
preparations.notes: Char adds smoke and roasted sugar notes; fresh green notes recede.

preparations.name: Roasted
preparations.notes: Dry heat concentrates sugars and adds roasted notes.

preparations.name: Toasted
preparations.notes: Nuts, spices, seeds or coconut; volatile top notes drop, bitterness if taken dark.

preparations.name: Caramelised
preparations.notes: Sugar taken to caramel; fresh fruit notes recede.

preparations.name: Fermented
preparations.notes: Lacto or yeast fermentation; fruit shifts towards wine-like notes.

preparations.name: Pickled
preparations.notes: Brined or vinegar-pickled; the brine itself works in savoury drinks.

preparations.name: Smoked
preparations.notes: Aroma-dominant: treat as one step more intense.

preparations.name: Dehydrated
preparations.notes: Top notes fade, sugars and acids concentrate; garnish or powder.

preparations.name: Powder
preparations.notes: As dehydrated with fast release; rims and dusting.

preparations.name: Syrup
preparations.notes: Carries the ingredient's aroma at roughly half to four fifths of fresh; sweet towards 5. 1:1 about 0.6 g sugar per ml, 2:1 about 0.9 g per ml.

preparations.name: Cordial
preparations.notes: As a syrup with added acid; bright top notes kept.

preparations.name: Shrub
preparations.notes: Fruit, sugar and vinegar; shelf-stable acidity for spirit-free drinks.

preparations.name: Oleo saccharum
preparations.notes: Citrus peel macerated in sugar; very aromatic.

preparations.name: Infusion
preparations.notes: Adds the infused ingredient's aroma at about 0.3-0.7 depending on time; bitterness and tannin if over-extracted (tea, peel, woody spices).

preparations.name: Tincture
preparations.notes: Concentrated extract used in drops or dashes; intensity 5.

preparations.name: Fat wash
preparations.notes: Spirit infused with a fat, chilled and strained; the fat's aroma carries over.

preparations.name: Clarified
preparations.notes: Agar, milk-wash or centrifuge; cloudy aromas drop, shelf-stable.

preparations.name: Reduction
preparations.notes: Simmered down; volatile top notes drop by about 0.3.

preparations.name: Purée
preparations.notes: Whole fruit blended: body and colour, rounder than juice.

preparations.name: Foam / whipped
preparations.notes: Aroma perceived first and lighter; air dilutes perceived sweetness.

preparations.name: Frozen / blended
preparations.notes: Cold suppresses aroma (about -0.2) and sweetness; recipes need roughly 10-20% more sugar.

preparations.name: Carbonated
preparations.notes: Carbonic bite lifts citrus and bitterness and releases aroma.

preparations.name: Brewed hot
preparations.notes: Hot extraction of coffee, tea or herbs; more aromatics and tannin.

preparations.name: Espresso
preparations.notes: Pressure extraction: concentrated, crema foams in shaken drinks.

preparations.name: Cold brew
preparations.notes: Long cold extraction: smoother, less acidic and bitter.

preparations.name: Saline solution
preparations.notes: A few drops suppress bitterness and lift fruit and sweetness.
